test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How long a person should have served as an advocate in a High Court to be eligible to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The office of appellate or supreme court justice is nonpartisan.
 
• To be eligible to serve in either position, a person must have practiced law for at least 10 years.
 
• An individual may be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court if
 
 
• He/She has been a Judge of a High Court for at least five years ("Appointment from the Bench")
 
• He/She has been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years ("Appointment from the Bar")
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on January 28, 1950.
 
• It succeeded in the Federal Court of India and was established under the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• Articles from 124 to 147 in Part V of the constitution deal with the organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers procedures of the Supreme Court.
